title: QUAX single-shell sapphire resonator with clamshell tuning, pseudo-TM030 at ~11.02 GHz

software.solver_type: driven modal (S-parameters; 'to get reliable C-factors'), Q from fitting transmission spectra; 0.1 deg steps 0-2 deg
software.boundary: copper sigma = 3.18e8 S/m (4 K, '5.48 x RT' for anomalous skin effect); RF gaskets modelled as bulk metal
software.mesh_notes: full 3D model incl. teflon pins and both on-axis antennas (Fig. 6a)

geometry.description: Copper cylinder (split longitudinally into two clamshell halves hinged at a fixed edge; one half rotates by the opening angle; end plates static) with one coaxial c-axis sapphire tube resting on the bottom plate; axial gap between tube top and top plate (0.73 mm at 4 K). Strong-port antenna on axis in the top plate, weak port on axis in the bottom plate. Teflon pins hold the tube.

gaps.parameter: clamshell hinge position, opening-angle definition, copper wall thickness, gasket geometry
gaps.proposal: hinge on the cylinder wall along the split line, rotate one half rigidly by theta, end plates fixed; gaskets as bulk metal (paper); sweep hinge location (inner wall vs outer surface) and compare df/dtheta with Fig. 7(a)

gaps.issue: not given; included in HFSS model
gaps.proposal: eigenmode without ports for f, C; antenna only for Q_L (not needed)

gaps.issue: shell inner radius not given and t inconsistent (3.97 vs 0.107 r_c = 3.01 mm)
gaps.proposal: skip as quantitative benchmark, or scan shell inner radius around 0.278 r_c for both t values and check if C=0.476 / Q=182000 is reached. exact model gives C = 0.469 at r1 ~10.6 mm, 10.98 GHz with t = 3.97 (max 0.489 with t = 3.01) -> start the shell-inner-radius scan at r1 ~10.6 mm.

inconsistencies.description: copper sigma(4 K) = 5.48 x sigma(RT) = 3.18e8 S/m: the factor 5.48 is the 1/R_s ratio of 2201.04223 Table I (207.04/37.75), not a sigma ratio; the equivalent sigma for R_s = 4.83 mOhm would be ~1.8e9 S/m (factor ~30)
inconsistencies.evidence: text Sec. V vs 2201.04223 Table I
inconsistencies.proposal: reproduce with the stated 3.18e8 S/m (that is what HFSS used); note Q_Cu would be ~2.4x higher with the 2201 R_s

inconsistencies.description: ALL three Table II simulated Q values are ~2x the analytic/semi-analytic value for the stated sigma = 3.18e8 S/m (R_s = 11.69 mOhm): pill-box 7.6e4 vs 3.78e4 (x2.01), ideal 1.82e5 vs 9.7e4 (x1.87), prototype (no gap) 3.28e5 vs 1.56e5 (x2.1). The measured Q ~1.75e5 AGREES with the analytic estimate, so the paper's 'phosphor-bronze gasket' explanation of the measured/simulated factor ~2 is suspect, and Fig. 7(b) simulated Q is likely also x2.
inconsistencies.evidence: TM010 at 11 GHz: a = 10.43 mm, L = 420 mm, R_s = 11.69 mOhm -> Q = Z0 chi01 / (2 R_s (1 + a/L)) = 3.79e4; TM030 dielectric rows from the exact layered model
inconsistencies.proposal: FLAG all 2410 simulated Q (Table II and Fig. 7b) as unreliable in absolute value; benchmark only Q ratios / angle trends. C: the pill-box C = 0.667 is 3.6% below the analytic TM010 0.6917 -> use ~4% C tolerance for 2410. F = (C V)^2 Q = 696 L^2 is consistent with the printed C and Q.

inconsistencies.description: prototype at 0 deg: Table II (Q=328000, C=0.235) vs Fig. 7 at 0 deg (Q~1.95e5, C~0.21)
inconsistencies.evidence: Table II vs digitized Fig. 7(b,c); Fig. 7 at 0 deg is perturbed by an intruder mode (text: TM_mn0, n=10)
inconsistencies.proposal: use Table II for an unperturbed axisymmetric prototype model; Fig. 7 for the 3D clamshell model

inconsistencies.description: Table II F for the ideal model (41300 L^2) implies V ~ 1.00 L, but pi 28.1^2 420 mm^3 = 1.04 L (-> 44800 L^2); prototype F=20000 vs (0.235 x 1.071 L)^2 x 328000 = 20800
inconsistencies.proposal: compare C and Q, not F

inconsistencies.description: Fig. 1 caption: L_c = 422.2 mm, r_c = 30 mm vs Table I r_c = 28.6 mm
inconsistencies.proposal: Fig. 1 is an illustrative model; use Table I

inconsistencies.description: thermal contraction in Table I: copper 0.436% (r_c, L_c) vs ~0.33% literature for Cu 293->4 K; sapphire 0.08%
inconsistencies.proposal: use Table I 4 K values as given

inconsistencies.description: ideal-design thickness: 3.97 mm (text) vs t = 0.107 r_c = 3.01 mm (Table II caption) vs rule 0.362 r/sqrt(eps) = 3.04 mm
inconsistencies.evidence: text Sec. II, Table II caption

inconsistencies.description: Table II prototype C = 0.235 (0.73 mm top gap, 0 deg) is not a precision target: in the axisymmetric model the TM030-like mode sits at an avoided crossing with high-order TM0np modes (C = 0 without the gap) within ~1e-4 in f
inconsistencies.evidence: benchmarks/records/cavity_repro_quax_clamshell_2410.json 'avoided_crossing_sensitivity': a 0.1-0.2 mm length change or a 0.01-0.02 eps change moves the largest-C mode between C = 0.15 and 0.28 and Q0 between 1.19e5 and 1.55e5, while the C sum of the modes within 6 MHz stays 0.285-0.289; an independent Q1 solver shows the same swing with the z mesh. The Fig. 7b Q at 0 deg (1.95e5, ~45 % below the neighbouring angles) suggests the same crossing in the HFSS model.
inconsistencies.proposal: do not use the 0.73 mm prototype C or the prototype Q ratios as precision targets; the no-gap C030 (0.3366, layered-exact) is the clean 2D benchmark

solver_class.reason: Closed clamshell (0 deg) with the top gap is axisymmetric (Table II prototype row, and the 0-deg point of Fig. 7 up to pins/antennas); any opening angle breaks the symmetry -> Fig. 7 needs 3D. Omitted in 2D: teflon pins (harmless for TM0n0); 0 deg only - the clamshell is not z-mirror-symmetric with the top gap.

priority_reason: Table II prototype row is a 2D-axisym check with a gap (field localisation) for f and C (~4% tolerance); ALL simulated Q (Table II, Fig. 7b) are ~2x the analytic value for the stated sigma -> Q only as ratios/trends. Tuning curves (Fig. 7) need 3D plus an unspecified hinge geometry.
